gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the UGREEN Nexode Air 65W comes in three hardware versions that share one model number, print and housing. Version 1 has no AVS, version 2 has AVS but does not hold 65 W, and only version 3 does both. Per techtest.org, the only measurable way to tell version 3 apart is its weight: 76 g, against about 82 g for the older two.
standout_why: I compared against Charge-Test (cited) and iThinkDifferent (cited), plus Apple Support 102574, ChargerLAB's iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max reviews, and LTT Labs (LTT returned HTTP 403, so I could not read it). Charge-Test gives AVS 'Yes' for the Nexode Air 65W Mini only 'with my tested version' and does not say how to identify that version. iThinkDifferent lists the Nexode Air 65W as AVS with no version caveat. ChatGPT told the shopper to 'check that you're buying the same AVS-capable revision' but could not say how. None of these pages mentions three versions, the shared model number, or the 76 g versus 82 g weight difference. Rivals cover part of my second finding: Charge-Test already says the Nexode Pro 160W X774 did not use AVS. What they lack is that ChargerLAB found the opposite on the same 5-port charger, and that techtest.org and Smartzone match Charge-Test's failure.
decides: This confirms the UGREEN Nexode Air 65W as a top third-party pick, but only if the shopper gets version 3. The row should say how to check: weigh it at 76 g, and the AVS listing UGREEN launched in October was burgundy, per Notebookcheck. Black and silver stock may be older units, per techtest.org. It also keeps our UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-port (ugreen-nexode-pro-160w-5-port) off the AVS list: three testers found the iPhone 18 Pro Max did not use AVS on it, and only ChargerLAB got AVS at about 52 W. The Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 (ours) and the Apple 40W Dynamic (A3351) both have tests showing working SPR AVS. Belkin WCH022 and ESR Xtend 45W rest only on what their makers say.

findings.label: Hardware versions sold under one model number
findings.value: Version 1: no AVS or USB PD 3.2, PPS 5–11 V up to 4.5 A, does not hold 65 W. Version 2: AVS and USB PD 3.2, PPS 5–11 V up to 5 A, does not hold 65 W. Version 3: AVS and USB PD 3.2, PPS 5–11 V up to 5 A and 5–21 V up to 3.25 A, holds 65 W.
findings.source_title: ACHTUNG! UGREEN Nexode Air 65W Mini: Es gibt drei Versionen – mit massiven Unterschieden (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2026-07-31)
findings.note: The table comes from Michael Barton's article, and his own unit was version 3. Barton attributes the claim that version 2 does not hold 65 W to measurements by a colleague named Jan. Barton writes 'Gleiche Modellnummer, gleicher Aufdruck, gleiches Gehäuse' (same model number, same print, same housing). The article body has no iPhone 18 test.

findings.label: How to identify version 3
findings.value: 76 g for version 3 against about 82 g for versions 1 and 2. Barton calls weight 'the only measurable clue'.
findings.source_title: ACHTUNG! UGREEN Nexode Air 65W Mini: Es gibt drei Versionen (techtest.org)
findings.note: Barton says the orange and Honkai: Star Rail editions are likely version 3, and black and silver are 'Glückssache' (luck of the draw) because they may be old stock. Colour is a pattern, not a guarantee. The article does not mention packaging or date codes.

findings.label: AVS revision launch and listing IDs
findings.value: AVS version launched at $39.99 in the US. Amazon US ASIN B0HG147M33; the German listing slug reads UGREEN-X860 (ASIN B0HFNB78WH). Burgundy colour matching the iPhone 18 Pro.

findings.note: Notebookcheck names no separate model number for the AVS revision. The $39.99 is a launch price from 2026-10-07, not today's price. I could not read today's price: UGREEN's US store returned 429 and 403, and amzcheck was blocked for B0HG147M33.

findings.product: Apple 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max
findings.label: Model number and cable condition
findings.value: Model A3351, tested with USB-C Charge Cable 1 m A3502 or 2 m A3503. Fast charge needs a '60W-capable USB-C cable'.
findings.source_title: Fast charge your iPhone - Apple Support (published 2026-10-22)
findings.note: The main text asks for USB-PD 3.2 with AVS, but the footnote says 'USB PD 3.1 (or better)'. Apple tells the shopper to use the cable from the box. Charge-Test labels the Apple adapter it tested 'A3352'. Apple names A3351.

findings.label: Bundled iPhone 18 Pro Max cable
findings.value: About 100 cm braided USB-C to USB-C, model A2795, no eMarker chip
findings.source_title: Charging Review of iPhone 18 Pro Max (ChargerLAB, 2026-10-12)
findings.note: A cable without an eMarker carries up to 3 A. The 18 V × 3 A AVS profile fits within that, and ChargerLAB measured the Apple 40W Dynamic at 17.35 V / 2.95 A / 51.23 W. EPR-only AVS (15–28 V) is not the SPR AVS the phone uses, per the same review.

findings.label: AVS claim and two-device split
findings.value: Belkin claims 'universal compatibility with the Adjustable Voltage Supply (AVS) protocol', with no SPR or voltage range stated. iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are in the compatibility list. Price $39.99 at belkin.com (SKU WCH022dqWH).
findings.source_title: UltraCharge Retractable GaN Wall Charger 67W, White (Belkin)
findings.note: Belkin gives charge times only for the iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max (17 Pro Max 0–50% in 23 minutes, internal testing), not the 18 Pro. Belkin AU FAQ article 337679 (https://www.belkin.com/au/support-article/?articleNum=337679, read 2026-11-27) gives the split with two devices as up to 45 W + 20 W. iThinkDifferent (cited) lists a 'Belkin 67W GaN Retractable' as PPS, not AVS. These are the maker's claims only.
